The blocker was downstream in the pre-existing E3 adjudication design, exposed only because the real published source was audited instead of the handoff summary.

defect.statement: adjudicate() verified metadata consistency and ledger provenance but never re-derived the detection event from persisted text. A candidate could CLAIM rule E3D-001 over an episode reading 'I like pizza.' and reach ADMIT_E3 -> evidence edge -> standing VERIFIED.

reproduction.result_before_repair: ADMIT_E3 / E3 / edge created / standing VERIFIED

defect.principle: The ledger proves WHERE the episode happened. It does not prove THAT the rule fired.
defect.why_the_suite_permitted_it: The E3 adversarial fixture manufactured rule_id=E3D-001 over episodes whose verbatim was the literal string 'placeholder', then expected ADMIT_E3 from later specimens. The fixture itself was the forgery.

law_established.status: ENFORCED in kernel; unratified as doctrine
law_established.statement: An adjudicator may confer E3 only when the candidate's detector event is reconstructable from its persisted source observations under the declared detector/rule version. Candidate metadata may IDENTIFY a detection result. It may never serve as PROOF that detection occurred.

kernel/e3.py: replay_rule() re-runs the declared rule's own patterns against the authoritative persisted verbatim.
E3D-004 (structural) reconstructs from >=2 E3D-001 matches across >=2 distinct persisted turns.
E3D-007, which has no replay procedure, FAILS CLOSED with RULE_REPLAY_UNSUPPORTED.
Candidate turn_id must equal the ledger turn_id of its source (TURN_MISMATCH).
observation.event must equal the rule's candidate_type (OBSERVATION_EVENT_MISMATCH).
matched_excerpt added; verified as a substring of the source (EXCERPT_NOT_IN_SOURCE).
detect() takes turn_id from the LEDGER, not its caller, and skips unledgered episodes — the detector cannot name a turn either.
db/005_e3_authenticity.sql: Trigger binding a claimed span to its source episode verbatim.
Trigger requiring ADMIT_E3 to rest on a source-bound span for lexical rules.

fixture_corrections_disclosed.why_disclosed: A corrected fixture changes what a previously-green suite was actually proving. Silently repairing them would convert a real coverage gap into an invisible one.
corrected: proof/test_e3_adversarial.py — fixture() episodes carried verbatim 'placeholder' while candidate() declared E3D-001 over them. Sources now genuinely satisfy the rule; ledger records the matching turn_id.
proof/test_e3_adversarial.py — the two LIFE-scope specimens now use source text that both fires E3D-001 and contains a life-claim, which is the real shape of that case.
proof/test_e3_live_postgres.py — ADMIT_E3 rows were built with no source binding; seed episodes and candidates now carry genuine correction text and a bound excerpt.

enforcement_asymmetry_declared.ddl_layer: db/005 enforces the weaker, rule-agnostic property that a claimed span must occur in its source. DDL cannot replay without duplicating the rule set, which would be a worse drift hazard than the gap it closes.
enforcement_asymmetry_declared.known_drift_hazard: One rule id (E3D-004) appears in DDL. Adding another structural rule to kernel/e3.py without amending that list would make it un-admittable at the database layer.
